title: Secure Protocol Services
headline: Trust is designed, not implied.
intro: Reliable systems are made from explicit identities, transport boundaries, policy and evidence—not confidence in an unfamiliar wire format.
summary: Alchemy secure communications work spans native HTTPS, XTP, mail protocols, RPC dispatch, authentication, cryptographic governance and service boundaries.

sections.heading: Separate transport from authority
sections.body: Encrypted transport can protect a connection, but it does not decide whether an actor may perform an operation. Authentication, authorisation, revocation and auditing remain independent requirements.

sections.heading: Multiple paths, one service meaning
sections.body: XTP work spans network layers; Connect Selector explores direct calls, RPC and Queue Fabric. Services must preserve their semantics across transports, rather than giving every protocol a separate business implementation.

sections.heading: Protocols should be testable
sections.body: TLS, SSH gateways, SMTP/IMAP and secure service endpoints need real negative testing, lifecycle management and recoverability. Development contracts should not be mistaken for commissioned production guarantees.
